choices.text: Plant cells have no mitochondria, because chloroplasts release all their energy
Plant cells have no mitochondria at night, but grow them during the day
Plant cells have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts, and respire day and night to release energy from sugar
Plant cells have mitochondria only in their roots

questions.explanation: The trap claim is: Plant cells have no mitochondria. Plant cells respire too, day and night: they have mitochondria as well - only the chloroplast is plant-only. Chloroplasts trap light energy in photosynthesis, but respiration in mitochondria is what releases that energy for cell activities, in plant and animal cells alike.

points.text: Chooses 'Plant cells have mitochondria as well as chloroplasts, and respire day and night to release energy from sugar'

questions.answer: Chloroplasts trap light energy to make sugar in photosynthesis; mitochondria release energy from that sugar as ATP in aerobic respiration, which continues day and night.
questions.explanation: The two organelles do different jobs: grana and stroma in the chloroplast build sugar (scene s4), cristae in the mitochondrion release its energy (scene s3). One does not replace the other.
